name: Proxima Centauri B findings (Collection)
description: Three objects were recovered from Proxima Centauri b, and all three produce sound continuously by means that have no counterpart among our instruments. B2311.1 was collected in the first week from scree above Kell Rille, logged as a nodule, and left in a crate for two years; what made anyone look at it again was that two independent clocks stored beside it had stopped drifting apart. It counts, and its sound is not a vibration at all but the list of moments at which something happened — rhythm, pitch and colour being one quantity in it, the rate of events, heard at three scales. Exposed to an outside pulse it eases towards it and never arrives; pushed harder it comes apart instead. B2311.22 came up from a dry cistern at the same rille — its sound is the vibration of its own connectedness, and energy put into it does not decay in place but travels through the structure. It did not come up alone: a second body lay beside it, and on raising the first the second changed pitch. B2311.67 was recovered 123 days later from a vault field of sixty-seven at the Sabik Terminator, each at the centre of its own void; it is a lattice rather than a body, perfectly ordered and never repeating, and its sound belongs to a category between tone and noise that no material we have made produces. B2311.104, the most recent finding, is a web rather than a body — conduits meeting at junctions on the same curved surface — and it does not answer being struck: it moves energy along itself as deep sound, continuously, and warming a conduit is how it is tuned, so to name a note is to command a temperature. The survey suspects it a fragment of a distribution grid, still carrying. None of the four has controls, and none has an off state. What the hand meets is a three-dimensional section through a four-dimensional body; move the section and a different part is simply present. Warming an object makes its own quantities begin to drive one another, along connections that are fixed and different in every specimen — a mechanism the survey suspects, but cannot show, to be the channel its builders spoke on. Field findings included, written in three registers they never mix: what has been established, what is suspected, and the questions the survey could not close.
